items.title: Chuck Israels interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 11, 2021
items.q: You were trying to understand and become conversant in the language of Bill Evans, Tommy Flanagan, Hank Jones, Sonny Clark were the piano players for example.

ctx.x: Did you listen to his music in that particular situation with the idea that what would I do if I was his bass player?

No. I didn’t get that far. I was — some people have, when I’ve talked to them about this have excused me, probably realistically, by saying, “Of course you were focused on a particular thing. You were trying to understand and become conversant in the language of Bill Evans, Tommy Flanagan, Hank Jones, Sonny Clark were the piano players for example. And the piano playing language of Monk was so — at least superficially — diametrically opposed to that, that you couldn’t take it in. You couldn’t see — that was…

All right. I wanted to ask you about, just a little bit about your time with Bill Evans. And I saw you say that when you got that gig, which of course was under unfortunate circumstances but nonetheless you felt you were going to get it.
